title: Unbuffered Tiny Writes (High-Frequency Syscall Overhead)
pattern: Performing repeated small-byte (e.g., 1-byte up to small block sizes) write operations directly to a physical file descriptor or network socket.
why_bad: Incurs massive kernel system call overhead (switching CPU execution privilege modes) and triggers physical write amplification and disk fragmentation.
detection: Low-level write system calls (`write()`, `syswrite()`) located inside high-frequency loops without intervening memory buffering.
counterexample: The write must be synchronous for real-time IPC or reliability guarantees. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Wrap the target file/socket in a buffered stream wrapper (e.g., `BufWriter` in Rust or C `setbuffer()`).
source: *Systems Performance*, Chapter 5 & 8 (p. 71 / p. 76 / p. 397) and *Understanding Software Dynamics*, Chapter 10 (p. 226).
